LAR.summary:
- **Sean McVay / Matthew Stafford (HC/QB)** — McVay said the biggest Week 1 issue was the pass game, and Stafford said the offense had only “probably two good drives”; the Rams went 2-for-9 on third downs and averaged -0.29 EPA per play. That points to a clear rebound push for the passing game, which would lift Stafford and the LAR pass-catchers if they sustain drives better this week. [4, 2]

- **Sean McVay’s 13-personnel package** — The Rams used 13 personnel on 36.8% of snaps in Week 1, even above their league-leading 2025 rate. That keeps this offense tilted toward heavy sets, which can cap wide receiver volume and keep the tight end rotation central in Week 2. [9]

- **The Giants’ run game** — New York ran for 165 yards in Week 1, while the Rams allowed 174 rushing yards and nearly 200 against San Francisco. If the Giants can stay on schedule, that could shorten the game and suppress Rams pass volume; if L.A. holds up better, it helps the Rams control the script. [5]

- **Aaron Donald (DL)** — Donald is trending toward a Week 2 debut, and the Rams’ pass rush already lacked much impact in Week 1. His return would raise the ceiling of the L.A. defense and could help the Rams get off the field quicker, but it does not directly add offensive volume. [7, 8]

- **Kam Kinchens (S)** — Kinchens did not practice with a hamstring injury, and the report says his absence could limit Quentin Lake’s usage while opening more work for Jaylen McCollough. If he sits, that shifts the Rams’ secondary rotation and makes McCollough the clearer playing-time beneficiary. [11]

CIN.summary:
- **Ja’Marr Chase (WR)** — Dan Pitcher said Cincinnati “didn’t throw him the ball enough,” and Zac Taylor said the staff has to keep finding ways to feature Chase after just four targets in Week 1; Taylor tied the quiet opener to an unusual first-half script and red-zone plan. That points to a stronger Chase target share and a higher ceiling this week. [5]

- **Bengals offense** — Cincinnati admitted it was slow in goal-to-go last week, and Houston’s ferocious pass rush is the specific matchup problem waiting Sunday. That raises the risk of stalled drives and suppressed TD efficiency for Joe Burrow, Chase and Tee Higgins, even if overall volume stays normal. [10]

- **Bengals defense** — Nico Collins is a real chance to miss Sunday after a hamstring injury, and Houston is already without Tank Dell and Jayden Higgins; Mitchell Tinsley could be elevated into action. That thins the Texans’ passing game and gives Cincinnati’s defense a slightly better turnover/sack environment. [11]

- **Shemar Stewart (DE)** — Stewart said he expects to make his season debut in Houston, and after back-to-back full practices he said he’d like to play around 30 snaps. That adds pass-rush juice for Cincinnati and modestly boosts the Bengals D/ST outlook against C.J. Stroud. [8]

- **Michael Carter II (S)** — Andrew Mukuba missed practice, and if he cannot play, Carter II would start next to Marcus Epps. That keeps the secondary in flux and is a small ding to Eagles D/ST stability if the safety pair is patched together late. [11]
